question: A 2-week old newborn is brought to the physician for a follow-up examination after the initial newborn examination showed asymmetry of the legs. She was born at term to a 26-year-old woman, gravida 3, para 2. Pregnancy was complicated by a breech presentation and treated with an emergency lower segment transverse cesarean section. The newborn's head circumference is 35 cm (13.7 in). She is at the 60th percentile for length and 75th percentile for weight. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The spine is normal. Abduction of the right hip after cupping the pelvis and flexing the right hip and knee causes a palpable clunk. The feet have no deformities. Ultrasonography of the hip determines the angle between lines along the bone acetabulum and the ilium is 50°. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.opa: Reassure the mother and schedule follow-up appointment in 4 weeks
options.opb: Immobilize the hips with a spica cast
options.opc: Perform closed reduction of the right hip
options.opd: Obtain an MRI of the right hip

paths: (Breech Presentation)-PREDISPOSES->(Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip)-CAUSES->(Disease)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(physiological aspects)-PROCESS_OF->(Hip structure)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Breech presentation -> increased risk of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) -> 80% CHAIN: Abnormal hip examination findings in newborn -> suspicion of DDH -> 70% CHAIN: Palpable clunk during hip abduction -> suggestive of hip dysplasia -> 60% CHAIN: Ultrasonography showing 50° angle between acetabulum and ilium -> indication for further management -> 70% CHAIN: Management of DDH often involves harness or closed reduction -> 70% CHAIN: Treat using a harness -> 80%
enhanced_information: The newborn's presentation with a palpable clunk during hip abduction and an angle of 50° on ultrasonography indicates developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). The most appropriate next step in management would be to treat using a harness, as this is a common approach in managing DDH. Immobilizing the hips with a spica cast or performing closed reduction may be considered in certain cases, but treating with a harness is a reasonable initial step.
